_comment: Queries an agent actually typed, with the task in front of it and no sight
of this corpus. Harvested verbatim from the trial transcripts in
research/scripts/agent-trial.ts — none were written for evaluation.
WHY THIS EXISTS. Every other eval query in this project is an observation
note, written by the same person who wrote the finding it is scored
against. That is honestly held out of the INDEX and not at all held out of
the AUTHOR, so it cannot measure the thing retrieval exists to solve:
two people describing one trap in different words. These can.
LABELS ARE JUDGEMENT AND ARE RECORDED AS SUCH. `gold` is the finding the
querier would have been glad to receive. `null` means nothing in the corpus
answers it — those are the valuable half, because a retriever is judged as
much on staying quiet as on hitting.
`repeats` records how many trials produced that query verbatim. Five agents
independently opening with the same sentence is evidence about the natural
phrasing of a task, so it is kept rather than averaged away.
One query named a finding by id, which means that agent had already been
shown it. It is kept, marked contaminated, and excluded from scoring.
Two negatives are marked `arguable` with the reasoning attached. The scorer
reports the sensitivity band both ways rather than picking the flattering one.
`selfReferential` lists records about this project's own retrieval and
measurement. They compete in this evaluation and cannot be written out of it:
cairn-0039 stopped quoting these queries verbatim and still intercepts three,
because it is ABOUT eval queries and its vocabulary is theirs.
The list is explicit rather than derived. A predicate on subject.name missed
cairn-0039 entirely — its subject is 'retrieval evaluation', not 'cairn' —
and reported no effect at all, which is worse than not decomposing.
Excluding them is never applied; it is printed alongside so the miss can be
split between the retriever and the ledger discussing itself.
HARVEST 2026-09-01 added eleven distinct queries (thirteen with repeats) from
four traps that had never been a scenario: cairn-0004, 0009, 0022, 0028.
Produced by npm run cairn:harvest over research/fixtures/harvest, labelled afterwards.
All eleven are answerable, and that is itself a finding about how agents ask.
Each trial issued about ONE query, at the start, about the task in front of
it. The unanswerable queries in the original set were mid-task asides — a
timezone parse, a NaN comparator — and these agents raised none. Query volume
and query kind are properties of the task, not of the agent.
HARVEST 2026-09-01b added fifteen UNANSWERABLE queries, which is the half that
had never been tested on new ground. Four debugging tasks in domains probed
first and confirmed uncovered — money rounding, retry and backoff, a
daylight-saving boundary, CSV encoding — each with several sub-problems and a
planted bug, because an agent that has to form a theory asks asides and asides
are where unanswerable queries come from. It worked: these tasks produced two
and three queries per trial where the first harvest produced one, including
genuine mid-task asides about Retry-After parsing and byte order marks.
None was built around anything in the corpus. Scored before being added here.

Kept null because the question is about the arithmetic rather than about the field's provenance, but a reader who called this answerable would not be wrong.
